payload.claim: `_candidate_constants` only checks whether the *matched span* (which, for a multi-line value like `NAME = (` followed by string segments on later lines, ends right after the first opening quote) overlaps an added line. If the declaration line and the first string segment are unchanged context but a later continuation line of the same multi-line literal is what the diff actually edited (e.g. `MESSAGE = (` / ` "line one "` stay as context while `-"line two"` / `+"line three"` is the real change), the match span never reaches the added line, so `_overlaps_added` returns False and no mutant is derived for that constant even though its value changed and a witness names it. This contradicts the stated behaviour that 'the constant is one the diff adds, or one whose line the diff changes' (problem statement, criterion 2). No test in this change exercises an *edited* (as opposed to wholly new) multi-line constant, so the gap produces no error and no test failure - it silently derives nothing.
